Definition: from G1073; a load (as filling), i.e. (specially) a cargo, or (by extension) wares:--burden, merchandise.
BiblicalUsage: gómos is a plain word for burden, merchandise. In Acts 21:3, the text says "for there the ship was to unlade her burden." In Revelation 18:11, the text says "for no man buyeth their merchandise any more."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that gómos matters because God's judgment is just, and it falls where it should — no one escapes it, and no one suffers it unjustly. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
